_about: Figures from reports, each read on the publisher's own page or PDF on the date given. Update by hand when a new edition is published.

hvs.source: NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development, 2023 New York City Housing and Vacancy Survey, Selected Initial Findings
hvs.quote: for renter households earning less than $70,000 (the median household income of renters), the typical rent-to-income ratio is 54.0 percent.

shelf.name: NYCgov Poverty Measure
shelf.publisher: NYC Mayor's Office for Economic Opportunity
shelf.edition: Key poverty trends in New York City, 2023-2024
shelf.headline: 24.3 percent of New Yorkers were in poverty in 2024, up from 23.1 percent in 2023 and 21 percent in 2022, and another 22.8 percent were near poverty.
shelf.method: The federal Supplemental Poverty Measure adapted to New York City: local housing costs, taxes, credits and noncash benefits counted.

shelf.name: Poverty Tracker
shelf.publisher: Columbia University Center on Poverty and Social Policy and Robin Hood
shelf.headline: 25 percent of adults and 27 percent of children were in poverty in 2024; 51 percent of adults were in families with at least one form of material hardship.
shelf.method: A panel survey that follows the same New York City households over time, measuring income poverty, material hardship and health.

shelf.name: Overlooked and Undercounted: Struggling to Make Ends Meet in New York City
shelf.publisher: Fund for the City of New York, with the University of Washington Center for Women's Welfare
shelf.headline: 46 percent of working-age households, about 1.2 million, lacked enough income to meet basic needs in 2024. The previous edition reported 50 percent.
shelf.method: A household budget, by borough and family type, for housing, child care, food, health care, transportation and taxes, compared with each household's income.

shelf.name: True Cost of Economic Security: Policy Implications for New York City
shelf.publisher: FPWA, using the Urban Institute's measure
shelf.headline: 62 percent of New Yorkers lacked the resources to cover their living costs in 2022, including 72 percent of families with children.
shelf.method: A household budget like the one above, built nationally by the Urban Institute and applied to the city.

shelf.name: The Unheard Third
shelf.publisher: Community Service Society of New York
shelf.headline: 26 percent of low-income New Yorkers had no rainy-day savings in 2023.
shelf.method: A yearly survey of New Yorkers, weighted toward low-income households. No results from later surveys have been published.
